title: Derived tensor comparison for arbitrary ringed topoi
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the universe of module sheaves, with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Equip it with a ring map $u^{-1}R\to S$. Write $D(R)$ and $D(S)$ for the unbounded derived categories of the abelian categories of sheaves of modules over these rings [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Module pullback is $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; $Lu^*:D(R)\to D(S)$ is its total left derived functor, computed by applying $u^*$ to K-flat resolutions with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Here a sheaf of modules is flat when tensoring with it is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. If $P$ is K-flat with flat terms, then $u^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms. Derived tensor is computed by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] of K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For all $F,G\in D(R)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
 Lu^*(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}G)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*F\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lu^*G
$$
in $D(S)$, natural simultaneously in $F$ and $G$.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, lines 3683-3724; and Tag 0G7E, label lemma-pullback-K-flat, lines 3507-3515

proof.text: Choose quasi-isomorphisms $P\to F$, $Q\to G$ with $P,Q$ K-flat with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$ represents $F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}G$, functorially on these representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $u^*P,u^*Q$ are K-flat with flat terms (this also proves the preservation clause of the item), without a flatness assumption on the ring map. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] they represent $Lu^*F,Lu^*G$. Applying the tensor descent statement over $S$, $\operatorname{Tot}(u^*P\otimes_Su^*Q)$ represents $Lu^*F\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lu^*G$.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, choice of representatives; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat

proof.text: The complex $T$ is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For an acyclic test complex $A$, reassociate the summands of the total tensors to identify $A\otimes_R T$ with $(A\otimes_RP)\otimes_RQ$. The associator on the $(a,p,q)$ summand is the ordinary tensor associator, defined by $(a_0\otimes p_0)\otimes q_0\leftrightarrow a_0\otimes(p_0\otimes q_0)$ and the balanced relations [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Distributivity over sums follows from the tensor universal property: a bilinear map from a direct sum is a family of bilinear maps from its summands. Both differentials have signs $1,(-1)^a,(-1)^{a+p}$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], so this is a chain isomorphism. The first inner tensor is acyclic by K-flatness of $P$, and tensoring it with $Q$ remains acyclic by K-flatness of $Q$. This is the elementary argument of Tag 07A2; no ringed-space tensor lemma is used.

Each $P^p\otimes_RQ^q$ is flat: tensoring a short exact sequence with it is, via the ordinary tensor associator, the composite of tensoring with $P^p$ and with $Q^q$, both exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The associator is the balanced pure-tensor map of Step 2 [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For each $n$, $T^n=\bigoplus_{p\in\mathbf Z}P^p\otimes_RQ^{n-p}$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This is a countable sum of flat sheaves, hence flat by the explicit countable-flat-sum clause of [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. Together with Step 2 this permits the comparison $\epsilon_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to identify $Lu^*(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}G)$ with $Q_S(u^*T)$.

source.place: Tag 07A4 proof; Tag 0G6Q, sites-modules lemma-tensor-flats; Tag 03EU, sites-modules lemma-colimits-flat (2)

proof.text: Pullback commutes with the sums used in the total complex. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] gives, for any family $(M_i)$ and any $S$-module $H$, $\operatorname{Hom}_S(u^*(\bigoplus_iM_i),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(\bigoplus_iM_i,u_*H)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,u_*H)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_S(u^*M_i,H)$. Thus $u^*(\bigoplus_iM_i)$ with coprojections $u^*\iota_i$ satisfies the coproduct universal property; its comparison with $\bigoplus_iu^*M_i$ is an isomorphism, natural in all $M_i$. In particular this applies to the countable family indexed by $p+q=n$.

For each $(p,q)$ invert the natural module isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to obtain $u^*P^p\otimes_Su^*Q^q\to u^*(P^p\otimes_RQ^q)$. Take their direct sum and compose with the coproduct isomorphism of Step 4. This gives a degreewise isomorphism $\beta:\operatorname{Tot}(u^*P\otimes_Su^*Q)\to u^*T$. Module naturality makes it commute with $d_P\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_Q$ separately. Pullback on modules is additive (its map is $1_S\otimes u^{-1}(-)$), so the scalar signs $(-1)^p$ in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] are preserved. Hence $\beta$ is a chain isomorphism, natural simultaneously in all complex maps $P\to P_1,Q\to Q_1$.

On the K-flat representatives define the comparison in the direction of the statement as $\epsilon_T$ followed by $Q_S(\beta)^{-1}$, with the representative identifications of Step 1. Every factor is an isomorphism by Steps 1--5. The transformation $\epsilon$ is natural on the homotopy category by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and $\beta$ is natural in each complex variable by Step 5, so this comparison is natural on $\mathcal P_R\times\mathcal P_R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], localizing $\mathcal P_R$ at quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(R)$, and natural transformations extend uniquely along this localization in both variables. Therefore these comparisons give a canonical natural isomorphism on $D(R)\times D(R)$. In particular the naturality equations for quasi-isomorphisms remain valid after inversion, which proves independence of the representative resolutions and simultaneous naturality for arbitrary derived morphisms. No localization of ordinary termwise pullback on all complexes is asserted.

split_report.summary: Repair: corrected the derived-pullback comparison and removed nonexistent ordinary pullback localization; proved site-level K-flat tensor closure directly; justified flat total terms using exactness and countable sums; derived coproduct preservation from a generic module adjunction; made two-variable descent explicit. Four smaller statement-only inputs, all searched afresh, replace the two returned nodes and add the missing adjunction and generic tensor descent.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes def-weil-pbc-four-corners statement clauses "Apply the canonical ordinary pullback/tensor comparison", "choose a K-flat representative", and "On these representatives the comparison is the natural tensor map". This is a foundational tool, not a replacement for any geometric step of sk-thm-properbasechange.

tool_uses.why: Uses only its generic countable direct sums of flat sheaves clause to check the total tensor has flat terms; the proper-base-change unit contains no such homological tool.
